pages.text: Every colony operates under a $(bold)tax policy$(). The policy you choose affects two things simultaneously: how much revenue your colony collects from taxes, and how that taxation influences your citizens' happiness.$(br2)Policies that raise more money cost you morale. Policies that keep citizens happy bring in less gold. The default is $(bold)Normal$(), which applies no modifiers.

pages.title: Changing Your Policy
pages.text: Only a colony owner or colony manager can change the tax policy.$(br2)$(bold)/wnt taxpolicy set <policy>$()$(br)Sets your colony's tax policy.$(br2)$(bold)/wnt taxpolicy$()$(br)Shows your current policy and its active modifiers.$(br2)$(bold)/wnt taxpolicy list$()$(br)Lists all available policies with their modifiers.

pages.title: When Policies Matter
pages.text: Policies interact with the random events system. Some events only trigger on high-revenue policies, and others only fire when happiness is already low. Holding a harsh policy for many tax cycles without managing happiness increases the chance of events like Guard Desertion or Labor Strike.$(br2)The War Profiteering event requires War Economy policy to be active.
